iut_type: General registration feasibility guidance (Seiko Solutions, exploring alternative controller/host stack options)
customer_question: As our internal discussions continue, other candidate options may come up. Just in case, can you tell us the cases where a new registration would NOT be possible?
question_variants: What are the disqualifying conditions for a new Bluetooth registration?
How can we evaluate future candidate controller/host stack combinations for registration feasibility?
actual_issue: The customer wanted a general framework for assessing registration feasibility for any future candidate hardware combination they might consider, rather than relying on case-by-case answers each time a new option came up.
plain_english_explanation: Rather than listing every possible disqualifying scenario (which would be impractically numerous and case-specific), Allion reframed the question as a positive checklist: a new registration is possible whenever all four of the following conditions are met — the controller and host stack to be implemented in the product already have their own QDID/DN registrations; the referenced QDID/DN registration is not subject to Withdrawal as of the registration date; the referenced controller/host stack's Core Specification doesn't differ significantly from what's actually being implemented; and the referenced QDID/DN registration doesn't contain any fatal cross-layer inconsistency. Allion offered to verify any specific candidate combination against these four conditions using a trial Qualification Workspace project once the customer identified one.
consultant_answer: There are too many specific disqualifying scenarios to list exhaustively, so it's more useful to frame this as what makes a new registration possible: all of the following need to be true — (1) the controller and host stack you're implementing already have their own QDID/DN registrations; (2) the referenced QDID/DN isn't subject to Withdrawal as of your registration date; (3) the referenced controller/host stack's Core Specification doesn't differ significantly from what you're actually implementing; (4) the referenced QDID/DN doesn't contain any fatal cross-layer inconsistency. Once you have a specific candidate combination in mind, let us know and we'll verify it against these conditions using a trial project.
decision_logic: Rather than enumerating disqualifying edge cases, registration feasibility is best communicated as a positive checklist of required conditions that can be applied consistently to any future candidate combination, with an offer to verify specific cases via a trial project rather than relying on abstract rules alone.
final_recommendation: When customers ask for a general 'what disqualifies registration' framework to evaluate future options themselves, provide the inverse positive-condition checklist instead of attempting to enumerate disqualifying scenarios, and offer concrete trial-project verification once specific candidates are identified.
risk_if_done_wrong: Attempting to exhaustively list disqualifying scenarios could give a customer false confidence that any scenario not explicitly listed is automatically safe, when the actual determining factors (QDID/DN registration status, spec compatibility, cross-layer consistency) need case-by-case verification regardless.
